lines.en: Freya, have you seen the news? A bridge in the city is going to be closed for repairs.
lines.pt: Freya, você viu as notícias? Uma ponte da cidade vai ser fechada para reparos.

lines.en: Yes, it was announced this morning. The work is said to take about six months.
lines.pt: Sim, foi anunciado esta manhã. Diz-se que as obras vão levar cerca de seis meses.

lines.en: Six months! The mayor is expected to speak about it tonight, isn’t she?
lines.pt: Seis meses! Espera-se que a prefeita fale sobre isso hoje à noite, não é?

lines.en: Probably. Two workers were injured last year while the bridge was being inspected.
lines.pt: Provavelmente. Dois operários foram feridos no ano passado enquanto a ponte estava sendo inspecionada.

lines.en: I read that the company has been criticised for ignoring safety rules.
lines.pt: Li que a empresa tem sido criticada por ignorar as regras de segurança.

lines.en: Apparently, the company had been warned twice before the accident happened.
lines.pt: Pelo visto, a empresa tinha sido avisada duas vezes antes de o acidente acontecer.

lines.en: If that is true, the contract should be cancelled. It is believed to have been awarded too quickly.
lines.pt: Se for verdade, o contrato deveria ser cancelado. Acredita-se que tenha sido concedido rápido demais.

lines.en: Careful. The story is still being investigated, and nothing has been proved yet.
lines.pt: Cuidado. A história ainda está sendo investigada, e nada foi provado ainda.

lines.en: You are right. We have been following it all week, and new details are published every day.
lines.pt: Você tem razão. Estamos acompanhando isso a semana toda, e novos detalhes são publicados todo dia.

lines.en: Shall we watch the live broadcast tonight? The mayor is expected to answer questions.
lines.pt: Vamos assistir à transmissão ao vivo hoje à noite? Espera-se que a prefeita responda a perguntas.

lines.en: Good idea. I will bring my notes, and we can compare the headlines tomorrow.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Levo minhas anotações, e amanhã podemos comparar as manchetes.

words.ex: To announce is to say something officially.
An injured person has been hurt.
To investigate is to look for the facts.
To criticise is to say what is wrong.
A headline is the big title of a story.
A broadcast is a program on TV or radio.

teach.goal: Ponte português → inglês com palavras úteis.
solo: Peça uma frase pessoal com 2 das palavras.
group: Palavras: announce, injured, investigate, criticise, headline, broadcast.
Aluno diz em português um uso real, depois a palavra em inglês.
extra90: Cada aluno escolhe a palavra mais útil e explica por quê.

facts.big: is/was being + particípio · has been + particípio · is said to…
facts.label: Passivo nas notícias
facts.sub: Em andamento: is being investigated. Presente perfeito: has been criticised. Relato: is said to…, is expected to…

facts.label: X is said to…
facts.sub: Use is said to… ou is believed to… para contar o que dizem sem afirmar que é fato: The work is said to take six months. É muito comum em notícias e relatórios.

facts.label: Is/was being + particípio
facts.sub: Use is being ou was being para ações em andamento: The story is being investigated. The bridge was being inspected. Mostra o processo, não o resultado.

compare.ask: The mayor is expected to speak.
compare.br: Em português, dizemos “diz-se que…” e “espera-se que…”.
compare.tip: Diga: “The mayor is expected to speak.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use X is said to… e He is expected to…

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

paragraphs: It is a rainy evening in Portland, and the city lights shine on the river. Bree and Marco meet at a living room to read the news. A big story about a bridge appears on every screen. They are friends, and they like to discuss current events. Marco has brought a newspaper and his tablet. Bree makes tea while they start to talk.

“Marco, have you seen the news? A bridge in the city is going to be closed for repairs.” says Bree. “Yes, it was announced this morning. The work is said to take about six months.” says Marco. “Six months! The mayor is expected to speak about it tonight, isn’t she?” says Bree.
